name: Coachbuilding
summary: The making of a car body by hand on a wood frame, and the fit of that body to a chassis that the client bought.
how: Build the body frame from ash timber and join it with metal brackets.
Beat the aluminium or steel panels over a wood form and fit them to the frame.
Fit the trim, the upholstery and the brightwork, then paint the body in many coats.

origin.note: Coach makers build horse-drawn carriages on a wood frame with leather and brass fittings. Early car bodies copy this work.

adoptions.via: The first cars carry carriage bodies on wood frames, with brass lamps and leather seats.
Coachbuilders make one-off bodies on bought chassis, and the client chooses the line, the colour and the trim.
Turin works beat light alloy bodies by hand for small series of grand tourers.
